title: SDK Robustness Playbook: id-key semantics, streaming resume, and adaptive backoff defaults
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Background:
Redwood SDKs (Python/TS/Go) currently have divergent retry and idempotency behaviors. This causes customer confusion, production incidents where duplicate effects occur, and brittle streaming resume semantics. We need a single playbook that provides: clear idempotency key semantics, safe backoff defaults per SDK and per call type (sync vs streaming), streaming resume token contract, telemetry/metrics and a migration/rollout plan.

Problem statement:
- Customers see different retry behaviors across languages and endpoints (e.g., some SDKs retry chat uploads more aggressively).
- Idempotency key usage is undocumented and lacks recommended TTL/dedupe windows, causing either duplicate side-effects or dropped retries.
- Streaming resumability lacks a cross-sdk contract (should we use op-level seq numbers, server tokens, or rely on chunk dedupe?).
- No standard metric names or SDK-level guards to detect runaway retries or excessive cost.

Goals:
1) Define opinionated, conservative defaults that minimize cost and duplicates while preserving availability.
2) Provide explicit idempotency key contract and sample implementations for Python/TS/Go.
3) Define streaming resume semantics including resume tokens, seq numbers, and dedupe window.
4) Standardize telemetry and sampling to enable product analytics and incident triage.
5) Provide rollout plan with feature flags and compatibility shims.

Non-goals:
- Automatic server-side de-duplication (server work planned separately).
- Rewriting transport libraries.

Proposed default retry/backoff matrix (rationale included inline):
- Short-duration idempotent RPCs (embeddings, simple generate):
  - max_attempts: 3
  - initial_delay: 100ms
  - multiplier: 2.0
  - max_delay: 2s
  - jitter: full (randomized between 0 and delay)
  - rationale: small number of retries reduces duplicate tokens/cost, handles transient network flakiness.
- Long/expensive idempotent RPCs (multi-turn chat generation, long-context generation):
  - max_attempts: 2
  - initial_delay: 250ms
  - multiplier: 1.8
  - max_delay: 3s
  - jitter: capped (avoid long tail)
  - rationale: fewer retries to bound cost; prefer graceful failure to silent duplicates.
- Non-idempotent RPCs (writes, billing-affecting ops):
  - max_attempts: 0 (no automatic retries by default)
  - rationale: require explicit idempotency-key or user-specified retry policy.
- Streaming/resumable operations (chunked uploads + tokenized streams):
  - handshake timeout and per-chunk retry: per-chunk max_attempts: 2, backoff initial 150ms
  - resume lexicon: prefer server-signed resume token, fallback to client seq numbers when token absent.

Idempotency key contract (recommended):
- Header: Idempotency-Key (string). SDKs should expose helpers to generate: uuidv4(), time-prefixed UUID, or deterministic operation fingerprint.
- Semantics: key scopes a logical operation (not a single transport packet). Reuse the same key for retries of the same user-visible operation.
- TTL/dedupe-window: default 5 minutes; configurable by request. Rationale: balances usability (clients rarely retry after many minutes) and server storage cost.
- Key rotation: SDK helper should optionally append SDK-version+timestamp metadata for debugging but server will ignore when deduping.
- Collision guidance: treat collisions (same key, different payload) as a user error; log and return 409 conflict when detected server-side.

Special rules for streaming and resumability:
- Resume token precedence: if server returns resume_token at any trimming point, subsequent reconnects MUST include resume_token in the initial request to request the suffix. This token is authoritative.
- Client seq numbers: when resume_token is unavailable, SDKs should maintain per-chunk seq numbers + chunk checksums. On reconnection, client includes last-acked-seq and server will accept idempotent replays up to the dedupe-window.
- Dedupe-window for streaming chunks: configurable but default 10 minutes. Shorter windows risk truncated streams; longer windows increase server storage.
- Partial acceptance semantics: server may acknowledge up to N bytes/chunks; client must only replay non-acked chunks.

Retryable error taxonomy (canonical categories):
- network.transient: transient TCP timeouts, DNS flakiness, connection resets. Retryable with normal backoff.
- transport.rate_limit: 429 with Retry-After header. Retry respecting Retry-After; treat as transient throttling.
- server.temporary: 5xx errors that indicate transient server load (502/503/504). Retryable but capped lower for expensive ops.
- server.permanent: 4xx errors that are client faults (400/401/403/404). Not retryable by default. 409 may be treated as non-idempotent conflict.
- model.resource_exhausted: model OOM or server-side resource limits. Retryable with longer backoff and exponential cap; include jitter.
- stream.resume_required: server signals that the stream cannot resume and client must restart operation (non-retryable).

Mapping to SDK behavior:
- Each SDK will ship a RetryClassifier component that maps http status + body codes into categories above. Teams should keep this classifier small and well-tested.
- Expose a clear override surface: client_builder.with_retry_policy(...) and per-call options. Default behavior must be documented and consistent across languages.

Telemetry and metrics (standardized names):
- sdk.retry.attempts (counter, tags: sdk.language, operation, category)
- sdk.retry.backoff.ms (histogram)
- sdk.idempotency.duplicates.detected (counter)
- sdk.stream.resume.attempts (counter)
- sdk.stream.resume.failures (counter)
- sdk.retry.blocked_by_policy (counter)
- Sampling: record full payloads only on sampled errors (default 0.1%) to protect PII.

SDK ergonomics: helper APIs (examples):
- Python (pseudo):
  client = RedwoodClient(retry_policy=RetryPolicy.defaults())
  with client.chat(idempotency_key=Idempotency.new()) as stream:
      stream.send(prompt)

- TypeScript (pseudo):
  const client = new Redwood({ retryPolicy: RetryPolicy.defaults('browser') });
  await client.generate({ idempotencyKey: idKey, model: 'x' });

- Go (pseudo):
  cli := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithRetryPolicy(DefaultRetryPolicy()))
  ctx := IdempotencyContext(ctx, genKey())
  resp, err := cli.Generate(ctx, req)

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Spec review and signoff (this ticket) — 1 sprint.
2) SDK implementations: add RetryClassifier + Idempotency helpers + telemetry hooks behind opt-in feature flag — 2 sprints.
3) Integration tests and chaos tests (network partitions, mid-stream interruptions) — concurrent with SDK work.
4) Gradual opt-in rollout: default OFF for 2 weeks while collecting opt-in telemetry, then switch ON with server-side compatibility checks.
5) Document and blog: publish cross-sdk playbook and sample snippets.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs (python/ts/go) have a RetryPolicy.defaults() implementation and an Idempotency helper.
- Streaming contract implemented with resume_token precedence and per-chunk seq fallback.
- Telemetry emitted for retry attempts and resume events.
- Cross-language test harness demonstrates consistent behavior for a set of golden scenarios (network blips, server 503, 429 with Retry-After, stream disconnect).

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Default dedupe window (5 minutes) is a compromise. Ops asked for longer for some enterprise customers. We expose config to increase on demand.
- Whether to enable automatic retries for some billing-impacting ops when Idempotency-Key is present. Current proposal: allow but with conservative max_attempts=1.

References & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLAT/pages/SDK+Resilience+Playbook (draft)
- Integration test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-resilience-harness (wip)
- Initial prototype PR (python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/412

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on whether the default matrices err on the side of safety. Ops and Sales have different tolerances — include risk notes for enterprise customers who will want longer windows.
